costNote: The consultants and delivery staff doing client work — 68 cents of every revenue dollar. Gross margin held at 32.0%.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning the work — pursuits and account teams. Bookings were $22.2B in the quarter (book-to-bill 1.2).

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running a ~800,000-person firm: management, finance, IT and offices.

otherDetail.label: Interest expense
otherDetail.note: Cost of debt — roughly cancels the interest income.

footerNote: Net income is the consolidated $2,034M; $1,991M was attributable to Accenture plc after noncontrolling interests.

oneTimers.label: No optimization charge this year
oneTimers.text: Q4 operating margin jumped 370bp partly because last year's fourth quarter carried $615M of 'business optimization' (restructuring) costs and this year's carried none. Against last year's adjusted margin, the gain was 20bp.

segments.name: Americas
segments.note: The largest market — US, Canada and Latin America. Grew 7% in dollars.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.note: Europe, Middle East and Africa. Grew 6% despite a small currency drag.

segments.name: Growth Markets
segments.note: Asia-Pacific and other faster-growing markets. Grew 3% in dollars, 7% in local currency.

sources.label: Accenture Q4 FY2026 earnings release — SEC EDGAR Ex-99.1 (8-K, Oct 1, 2026)

takeaways.text: Q4 EPS rose 46% — flattered by comparison with a year-ago quarter that absorbed $615M of restructuring. Versus adjusted EPS last year, growth was 9%.
takeaways.title: EPS up 46% (with an easy comparison)

takeaways.text: Full-year bookings hit $84.5B with a record 141 quarterly client bookings of $100M+; Q4 bookings were $22.2B, led by managed services at a 1.4 book-to-bill.
takeaways.title: Bookings stayed strong

takeaways.text: Fiscal 2027 guidance: revenue growth of 3–6% in local currency and GAAP EPS of $14.39–14.81 — steady, not spectacular, with at least $9.5B of planned shareholder returns ($11.5B in FY26).
takeaways.title: FY27 outlook is measured

verdict: Accenture closed its year above guidance: 6% growth, a 370bp margin jump (against a restructuring-hit quarter) and record bookings.
